vignette: A 45-year-old alcoholic is admitted confused and unsteady. He cannot abduct either eye and has coarse nystagmus. A junior doctor gives intravenous glucose and he becomes more drowsy.
stem: What should have been given first, and which structures are being damaged?

options.text: Thiamine; the mammillary bodies and periaqueductal region

explanation: Confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia in a malnourished alcoholic is Wernicke encephalopathy, a thiamine-dependent injury of the periventricular structures around the third and fourth ventricles and aqueduct; glucose without thiamine precipitates or worsens it, and the mammillary body damage leaves Korsakoff amnesia.
